title: Re-pinning the primary model
text: The controller remembers each model Deployment's identity and a hash of its spec. If the primary Deployment is edited (for example an env var), the hash no longer matches and **every** controller action, including recover, is refused until a human approves the new hash. This is a safety gate, not a bug. The gate only opens if the controller is `qwen-ready`,

title: Changing a model setting safely
text: Model settings live in the manifest (for example `manifests/10-infrastructure/llm/llama-cpp-swift-qwen38.yml`). The sequence is: edit in Git → `kubectl diff -f <manifest>` and confirm only the intended lines differ → apply at a **quiet time** (the model restarts, taking a few minutes) → re-pin → verify `qwen-ready` and a real answer → keep the old value read

title: Installing or removing models
text: Use **LLM Lab → Model Manager** (`https://glance.internal.homelab.example/model-manager/`). Paste a Hugging Face URL, choose the revision and variant, check the exact size, then **Download & set up**. *Downloaded*, *configured*, *registered* and *tested* are separate states. Removal unregisters and keeps files unless you explicitly confirm quarantine.

title: Artex user guide
text: Artex is an autonomous agent that executes shell commands, drives a real browser and sends network traffic on your behalf. Use it only against systems you own or have explicit written authorization to test. This deployment does not change that: it only constrains where Artex can run and who can reach it.

title: What this is

text: **System → Intercept** is the one setting that determines whether Artex can act without you watching. Every tool call a worker/planner/mainagent wants to make is checked, in priority order (highest first), against your rules before it runs: Match target What it matches Match type `tool_name` Which tool is being called (e.g. a shell runner, an HTTP request to
